Formula: Kepler's Third Harmonic Law of Planetary Motion
Exact Expression: T^2 = \frac{4\pi^2}{G(M + m)} a^3
Definitions: Astronomical law stating that the square of the orbital period of a planet is directly proportional to the cube of the semi-major axis of its orbit.
Derivation/Reference: Johannes Kepler, Harmonices Mundi (1619); Isaac Newton derived from law of universal gravitation in Principia (1687)
Example: Earth orbit around Sun: a = 1.0 AU, T = 1.0 year -> T^2 / a^3 = 1.0 yr^2 / AU^3 for all Solar System planets
Domain: celestial_mechanics
Assumptions: Two-body gravitational system subject to inverse-square central force; Negligible perturbations from other planetary bodies
Common Errors: Neglecting central body mass M in binary systems of comparable masses (e.g. binary neutron stars)
subject: Kepler's Third Harmonic Law of Planetary Motion
